issues.title: Onboarding: set up, run verify, walk the demo path
issues.body:
Everyone does this in week 1. Follow the setup steps in CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Done when

- [ ] Claude Code installed and signed in
- [ ] `npm run verify` passes on a clean clone
- [ ] Demo path walked locally with the sample company: open a job, move a candidate to an offer, hire, onboarding checklist, pay run
- [ ] A demo company made on the live server; careers page and Lark tried there
- [ ] Asked Claude Code for a tour of your workstream's code, and checked its answers against the code
- [ ] Your workstream's first pull request merged by the end of week 1

issues.title: Threat model for sign-in, invites and the careers form
issues.body:
Write `docs/THREATS.md`: what an attacker could want from First Twenty and how they could try to get it.

Start from `server/src/auth.ts` (sign-in, sessions, the login rate limiter), `server/src/workspaces.ts` (sign-up and invites) and `server/src/careers/` (the public apply form).

The repo is public, so `docs/THREATS.md` names gaps, not working attacks. Any vulnerability you find goes through `SECURITY.md` (private vulnerability reporting), never a public issue or pull request.

## Done when

- [ ] Assets listed (logins, company data, careers applications, the assistant's budget)
- [ ] Each entry point listed with the defenses already in the code, each with a file reference
- [ ] The five biggest gaps ranked, each with a proposed fix (they become issues; anything exploitable is reported privately instead)
- [ ] Reviewed by a teammate and the product owner

issues.title: Roles the server enforces for pay and personal records
issues.body:
Today every login is created as an admin (`server/src/workspaces.ts`), and the manager and employee limits live only in the browser (`src/domain/access.ts`, `useViewer()`), which is a preview, not security.

This issue covers pay and personal records only. Roles for every other record are stretch work, filed as a new issue once this one is merged.

## Done when

- [ ] A design note approved in a Wednesday session before the code starts: roles, what each may read and write in pay and personal records, how sync filters those records per login (see `docs/SYNC.md`)
- [ ] Each login has a role (admin, manager, employee); an invite picks the role
- [ ] For pay and personal records, the server sends each login only what its role may read, and refuses writes it may not make
- [ ] Tests try each forbidden read and write on those records, and fail if the check is removed
- [ ] The UI's "preview, not security" notes are updated wherever the server now enforces the role, and kept everywhere else

issues.title: Password reset by email
issues.body:
There is no way to recover a forgotten password today.

## Done when

- [ ] A reset link that is single-use, expires, and is stored hashed (follow the invite tokens' pattern)
- [ ] Requests are rate-limited and never reveal whether an email has a login
- [ ] Signing in after a reset ends the login's other sessions
- [ ] Tests cover expiry, reuse, and the rate limit
- [ ] Email delivery choice agreed with the product owner (it costs money and needs a sending domain)

issues.title: Pre-release security check and fixes
issues.body:
Any vulnerability found goes through `SECURITY.md` (private vulnerability reporting), never a public issue or pull request. The results pull request records only what is safe to make public.

## Done when

- [ ] `docs/SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md`: the checks to run before each release (dependencies, headers, open ports, backups, secrets, the threat model's gaps)
- [ ] Run in weeks 7 and 8, with the results recorded in a pull request and every finding fixed or filed (anything exploitable through `SECURITY.md`)

issues.title: Encrypted storage and a real domain
issues.body:
Stretch work: only in spare time before week 6, once the core work is on track. Done together with the product owner, who holds the server access.

## Done when

- [ ] A runbook in `docs/SERVER.md`: moving the database to an encrypted volume, with the backup and restore steps tested on a copy first
- [ ] A runbook for moving from the sslip.io address to a real domain (DNS, certificates, careers hosts)
- [ ] The product owner has carried out both, and the live site still passes its health check

issues.title: New York: pay range in job posts
issues.body:
California already requires a pay range in job posts, and the app handles it. Add New York's rule for jobs based there.

## Done when

- [ ] The rule's text, thresholds and effective date come from an official New York source, opened and read, recorded in `docs/LAW.md` with the link and the date checked
- [ ] A New York-based job gets the same pay-range check and posting wording California jobs get, adjusted to New York's rule
- [ ] Tests cover a New York job with and without a range
- [ ] Nothing about California changes

issues.title: New York rule pack
issues.body:
Rules cover California employers only today (see `ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Legal rules by work state").

## Done when

- [ ] A design note approved in a Wednesday session before the code starts: each New York rule a 1-to-20-person company meets (thresholds, notices, final pay, leave), each with its official source
- [ ] The rules implemented with tests, each recorded in `docs/LAW.md`

issues.title: Employees working in New York for a California company
issues.body:
## Done when

- [ ] A person's work state drives their checklists, notices, final pay and leave rules, for California and New York
- [ ] The threshold counts (5, 15, 20 employees) count people the way each rule's source says
- [ ] Tests for a California company with a New York employee, and the reverse

issues.title: 25 test questions for Lark, with correct answers
issues.body:
Lark is the in-app assistant (`server/src/assistant/`). Nobody measures whether its answers are right.

## Done when

- [ ] 25 questions an admin of the sample company might ask, each with the correct answer worked out from the sample data (`docs/SAMPLE.md`)
- [ ] A mix: simple lookups, legal deadlines, counts, questions it should refuse or answer with care (other people's pay for non-admins, legal advice)
- [ ] Stored as a test fixture the scoring suite can read

issues.title: A test suite that scores Lark's answers
issues.body:
## Done when

- [ ] A runner that asks Lark each fixture question and scores the answer (exact facts checked by code; wording judged against written criteria)
- [ ] Runs against the fake model in CI (no cost), and against the real model only on demand, under a set spend cap
- [ ] A report: accuracy, refusals that should have been answers, answers that should have been refusals
- [ ] A baseline score recorded, so later prompt or tool changes can be compared

issues.title: Founder usability sessions
issues.body:
## Done when

- [ ] Before the sessions, the advisor reviews the session script and consent form
- [ ] If any results will be published as research, the advisor checks whether IRB review applies
- [ ] Sessions with three founders. Each participant signs the consent form and uses only a demo company to post a job, hire and prepare a pay run
- [ ] Notes kept out of the repo, with no personal details; the top issues filed, each with the task tried and what happened, and nothing that identifies the person or their company
- [ ] The top fixes merged, each pull request linked here
